notes: Author of The Colony (2016), son of Lowell Pierson Beveridge Sr. In a 2012 recorded oral history Pete personally identified himself, described summers on shared North Haven family property, and recounted strong opposition from his father's seven siblings to his relationship with filmmaker Hortense (“Tee”) Sie. The couple married in January 1954 at St. Philip's Episcopal Church in Harlem, with his parents' and brother's attendance and the parents' ultimate blessing, despite the wider family's objections. He discussed his progressive organizing at Harvard. Earlier search-summary claims of a 1953 wedding, a complete disowning by his parents, or an exactly 20-year exile are not supported by this original interview. The family property's later sale is mentioned in Lowell Sr.'s 1960 Harvard report but cannot be causally linked to the marriage from that report alone. Do not publish inferred living relatives, current addresses or private contacts.
evidence_status: First-person 2012 oral history, 1960 father-authored Harvard family report, and 1991 diocesan memorial establish the distinct author and 1954 marriage; any precise exclusion duration remains unverified

notes: Filmmaker Hortense 'Tee' Sie Beveridge (1923–1993), who worked as a film editor and documentarian. Pete Beveridge described their relationship, their interracial marriage in January 1954 at St. Philip's Church in Harlem, and historical family opposition in a 2012 public oral-history interview; his parents and brother attended. The surname Sie and earlier marriage status appear in the 1960 Harvard class report. The Smithsonian identifies her role in the documentary South Africa Uncensored (1951). This account does not establish a 1953 wedding or a specifically 20-year banishment from North Haven.
evidence_status: Public filmmaker identity and life years supported by Smithsonian catalog; spouse relation documented as of 1960 by father-in-law's Harvard record; birth day from published scholarly history
